label: Last two copy outputs of long (L=9) sequences, token-dependent
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (t > L); never during original input or on the <DEL> step. Activity is concentrated at the end of the copy: 78% of mass is on the last two outputs (to_go <= 1) and 90% on the last three. It is strongly biased toward long sequences: L=9 holds 74% of the mass, and t=16-17 (the last two outputs of L=9) have 15-21% firing rates. The strongest activations are the final output steps of L=9 sequences. Even within that context it fires on only about 18% of steps (dev F1 0.26, mass recall 0.60). Which steps fire depends on token identity in ways no simple predicate captured: it prefers outputs h/2/i/u (about 6.7x lift for h and 2) and previous inputs u/n/j, but adding token sets did not improve F1. Short sequences (L=4-5) almost never fire; L=3 fires weakly at step 5.
